orgs.name: Machine Intelligence Research Institute (MIRI)
orgs.description: The original AI alignment research nonprofit, founded in 2000. After two decades of agent-foundations research, MIRI now concentrates on communications and policy work aimed at stopping the race to superintelligence. Its leadership wrote the 2025 book If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies.

orgs.name: Center for AI Safety (CAIS)
orgs.description: Research and field-building nonprofit focused on reducing societal-scale risks from AI. Runs technical research, compute support for safety researchers, courses and fellowships, and organized the 2023 Statement on AI Risk.

orgs.name: Center for Human-Compatible AI (CHAI)
orgs.description: Stuart Russell's research center at UC Berkeley. Works on reorienting AI research toward systems that are provably beneficial, including assistance games and value learning. Gifts are processed through UC Berkeley.

orgs.name: FAR.AI
orgs.description: Frontier alignment research nonprofit working on robustness, interpretability and model evaluation. Also runs events and programs such as the Alignment Workshop series that connect researchers and policymakers.

orgs.name: Redwood Research
orgs.description: Applied alignment lab best known for pioneering AI control: techniques for getting useful, safe work out of models that might be misaligned. No public donation page; reach out through the website.

orgs.name: Alignment Research Center (ARC)
orgs.description: Theoretical alignment research nonprofit founded by Paul Christiano. Works on formal approaches to explaining and verifying model behavior, such as heuristic explanations and eliciting latent knowledge.

orgs.name: Eleos AI Research
orgs.description: Research nonprofit on AI sentience and welfare. Studies whether and when AI systems might warrant moral consideration and advises labs on welfare-relevant practices.

orgs.name: METR
orgs.description: Model Evaluation and Threat Research (formerly ARC Evals). Measures frontier model capabilities, especially autonomous and long-horizon task performance, and runs pre-deployment evaluations with AI developers.

orgs.name: Palisade Research
orgs.description: Studies offensive and dangerous capabilities in current AI systems, including shutdown resistance and hacking, and turns the findings into concrete demonstrations for policymakers and the public.

orgs.name: AI Futures Project
orgs.description: Forecasting nonprofit led by Daniel Kokotajlo, authors of the AI 2027 scenario. Produces scenario forecasts, tabletop exercises and policy recommendations about the trajectory of AI.

orgs.name: AI Impacts
orgs.description: Researches decision-relevant questions about the future of AI, including its long-running Expert Survey on Progress in AI.

orgs.name: MATS
orgs.description: Research fellowship that pairs emerging researchers with established mentors in alignment, interpretability, governance and security. One of the field's main talent pipelines, with cohorts in Berkeley and London.

orgs.name: Lightcone Infrastructure
orgs.description: Runs LessWrong, the AI Alignment Forum and the Lighthaven campus in Berkeley, core shared infrastructure for AI safety discussion and events.

orgs.name: Manifund
orgs.description: Open grantmaking platform. Donors can fund individual AI safety projects directly or give to regrantors who move money quickly to early-stage work.

orgs.name: Transformative AI Fund (EA Funds)
orgs.description: EA Funds' AI-focused grantmaking fund and successor to the Long-Term Future Fund, which has closed and no longer accepts donations. Donors outside the UK and Netherlands give via Every.org; UK and NL donors give via Giving What We Can.

extraLinks.label: UK / NL donors (Giving What We Can)

orgs.name: Centre for the Governance of AI (GovAI)
orgs.description: Research organization studying how to govern advanced AI, from compute governance to international institutions. Runs well-regarded summer and winter fellowships.

orgs.name: Emerging Challenges Fund (Longview)
orgs.description: Longview Philanthropy's pooled fund for emerging global catastrophic risks, with AI safety and governance as its main focus. Grants are recommended by Longview's research team.

orgs.name: BlueDot Impact
orgs.description: Runs free online courses in AI safety and AGI strategy that have trained thousands of people entering the field, plus project sprints and rapid grants for alumni.

orgs.name: ControlAI
orgs.description: Campaign organization working to prevent the development of artificial superintelligence. Briefs legislators, drafts model legislation and runs public campaigns in the UK and US.

orgs.name: CeSIA (Centre pour la Sécurité de l'IA)
orgs.description: France's main AI safety organization. Combines French and EU policy work with research and education, including university courses and public outreach in French.

orgs.name: PauseAI
orgs.description: Grassroots movement calling for an international pause on frontier AI development until it can be made safe. Organizes protests, lobbying and local chapters in many countries.

orgs.name: Apart Research
orgs.description: Global research accelerator that runs AI safety hackathons and research sprints, then supports promising teams through fellowships to publication.

orgs.name: Future of Life Institute (FLI)
orgs.description: Works to steer transformative technology away from large-scale risks. Active in EU and US AI policy, publishes the AI Safety Index, and makes grants.

orgs.name: Institute for AI Policy and Strategy (IAPS)
orgs.description: Nonpartisan think tank producing policy research on AI security, compute and international strategy, and running an AI policy fellowship.

orgs.name: Americans for Responsible Innovation (ARI)
orgs.description: Bipartisan policy advocacy group working with Congress and federal agencies on AI safety and accountability legislation.

orgs.name: Encode AI
orgs.description: Youth-led advocacy organization (formerly Encode Justice) that has co-sponsored state AI safety bills and mobilizes young people on AI policy.

orgs.name: Horizon Institute for Public Service
orgs.description: Fellowship program that places people with emerging-technology expertise into US federal and congressional roles.

orgs.name: AI Safety Research Fund
orgs.description: Grantmaker focused on early-stage, underfunded and unconventional AI safety research, including researchers outside the usual funding networks.

orgs.name: AI Risk Mitigation (ARM) Fund
orgs.description: Pooled fund where experienced grantmakers evaluate and fund AI safety projects. Donations are routed through Effective Ventures Foundation USA.

orgs.name: AI Safety and Governance Fund (AISGF)
orgs.description: Nonpartisan 501(c)(4) that explains AI existential risk to the public, mainly through an educational chatbot that walks people through the arguments and common objections.

orgs.name: The Midas Project
orgs.description: Watchdog that tracks and publicizes changes to AI companies' safety commitments and governance, including OpenAI's restructuring.

orgs.name: AI Safety Camp
orgs.description: Long-running online research program where small teams work on AI safety projects for several months under a project lead. Low-cost entry point into the field.

orgs.name: AISafety.info (Stampy)
orgs.description: Volunteer-built, plain-language FAQ on AI existential risk, with an AI assistant trained on the alignment literature. Funds support distillation fellowships and the site.

orgs.name: AISafety.com
orgs.description: Hub that maps the AI safety ecosystem: courses, events, jobs, funding sources and communities, plus a donation guide.
